summary.text: The counterexample is $800322180$: monotonicity and $\binom{33}{16}>800322180$ force both binomial indices in any putative representation to lie in $\{0,\ldots,15\}$. For each of the resulting 256 pairs, a finite factorization computation finds a prime congruent to $3\pmod 4$ occurring to an odd exponent in the residual, so the residual cannot be a sum of two squares.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
B(k)=\binom{2k+1}{k}
\]
and put
\[
N=800\,322\,180.
\]
We will prove that there are no nonnegative integers \(a,b,c,d\), even without imposing \(a\le b\), for which
\[
N=a^2+b^2+B(c)+B(d).
\]
In particular there are none satisfying both \(a\le b\) and \(c\le d\), so the number of representations counted by A303639 is zero at \(N\). Since \(N>1\), this disproves the conjecture.

We use the following standard consequence of the sum-of-two-squares theorem.

**Sum-of-two-squares obstruction.** If a positive integer \(m\) contains a prime \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) to an odd exact exponent, then \(m\) is not a sum of two integer squares.

Here “to the exact exponent \(e\)” means that \(p^e\mid m\) but \(p^{e+1}\nmid m\). For completeness, the obstruction can be proved directly. Suppose that \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) is prime and that
\[
p\mid x^2+y^2.
\]
If \(p\nmid y\), then \(xy^{-1}\) modulo \(p\) would be a square root of \(-1\). But if \(t^2\equiv-1\pmod p\), then, because \((p-1)/2\) is odd,
\[
t^{p-1}=(t^2)^{(p-1)/2}\equiv-1\pmod p,
\]
contrary to Fermat’s little theorem. Thus \(p\mid y\), and then \(p\mid x\) as well. Consequently, whenever \(p\mid x^2+y^2\), both \(x\) and \(y\) are divisible by \(p\), so \(p^2\mid x^2+y^2\). Dividing both squares by \(p^2\) and repeating shows that the exact exponent of \(p\) in a nonzero sum of two squares must be even. This proves the obstruction.

We next bound the possible binomial indices. The first relevant values of \(B(k)\) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
k&0&1&2&3&4&5&6&7\\ \hline
B(k)&1&3&10&35&126&462&1716&6435
\end{array}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
k&8&9&10&11&12&13&14&15\\ \hline
B(k)&24310&92378&352716&1352078&5200300&20058300&77558760&300540195.
\end{array}
\]
The sequence \(B(k)\) is increasing. Indeed,
\[
\frac{B(k+1)}{B(k)}
 =\frac{\binom{2k+3}{k+1}}{\binom{2k+1}{k}}
 =\frac{(2k+3)(2k+2)}{(k+2)(k+1)}
 =\frac{2(2k+3)}{k+2}>1.
\]
Moreover,
\[
B(16)=\binom{33}{16}=1\,166\,803\,110>N.
\]
Therefore, in any proposed representation of \(N\), neither \(c\) nor \(d\) can be at least \(16\), since all four summands are nonnegative. Hence
\[
0\le c,d\le15.
\]
Because the representation requires \(c\le d\), only the \(136\) pairs \(0\le c\le d\le15\) remain.

For each such pair define the remainder
\[
R_{c,d}=N-B(c)-B(d).
\]
The following finite arithmetic table gives, for every remaining pair, a prime occurring in \(R_{c,d}\) to an odd exact exponent. In row \(c\), the entries correspond successively to
\[
d=c,c+1,\ldots,15.
\]
An entry \(p\) means that the exact exponent of \(p\) in \(R_{c,d}\) is \(1\); an entry \(p^e\) means that its exact exponent is the displayed odd integer \(e\).

\[
\begin{array}{c|llllllllllllllll}
c&\multicolumn{16}{c}{\text{entries for }d=c,c+1,\ldots,15}\\ \hline
0&647&163&67&3&23&467&223&991&7&3&23&3&887&26905651&7&1999\\
1&3^3&643&19&3&3^7&3&3&78607&27594131&3&31&11&3&3&3\\
2&11&3&200080511&23&284003&4326031&19&3&399984727&3&79512187&127&2819&7\\
3&7&7&7&43&5843&3&7923067&7&7&3&23&23&23\\
4&3&3&719&3&563&200057419&3^3&7&7&3&3&3\\
5&3^3&3&3&12504647&23&3&7&7&3&3&3\\
6&3&19&7&7&3&139&227&11&3^5&67\\
7&3&199&31&31&3331&139&3&3&3\\
8&689891&3&223&3&59&11&7591&19990307\\
9&19&887&19&3&11&19&19\\
10&3&19&7&19&3^3&19\\
11&7&3&19&19&19\\
12&7&19&19&19\\
13&3&3&3\\
14&3&3\\
15&3
\end{array}
\]

Here is the precise arithmetic content of the table. For the entry in position \((c,d)\), if it is written \(p^e\), direct integer division gives
\[
p^e\mid 800\,322\,180-B(c)-B(d),
\qquad
p^{e+1}\nmid 800\,322\,180-B(c)-B(d).
\]
All the displayed exponents are odd. The distinct primes used in the table are
\[
\begin{gathered}
3,7,11,19,23,31,43,59,67,127,139,163,199,223,227,467,563,643,647,719,887,991,\\
1999,2819,3331,5843,7591,78607,284003,689891,4326031,7923067,12504647,\\
19990307,26905651,27594131,79512187,200057419,200080511,399984727.
\end{gathered}
\]
Each of these integers is congruent to \(3\pmod4\). Their primality follows by trial division by primes not exceeding their square roots; no such prime divisor occurs. Thus every entry really supplies a prime congruent to \(3\pmod4\) with the asserted odd exact valuation. The divisibility and nondivisibility checks use the displayed list of \(B(k)\)-values and ordinary integer division. For illustration of how the rows are read:

* At \((c,d)=(0,0)\),
  \[
  R_{0,0}=800322180-1-1=800322178,
  \]
  and \(647\mid R_{0,0}\) but \(647^2\nmid R_{0,0}\).
* At \((1,1)\),
  \[
  R_{1,1}=800322180-3-3=800322174,
  \]
  and \(3^3\mid R_{1,1}\) but \(3^4\nmid R_{1,1}\).
* At \((1,5)\),
  \[
  R_{1,5}=800322180-3-462=800321715,
  \]
  and \(3^7\mid R_{1,5}\) but \(3^8\nmid R_{1,5}\).
* At the final pair \((15,15)\),
  \[
  R_{15,15}=800322180-2(300540195)=199241790,
  \]
  and \(3\mid R_{15,15}\) but \(9\nmid R_{15,15}\).

These examples also show the role of every table entry: it is not merely a divisor, but certifies an odd *exact* exponent. The same two integer-division checks are made for each of the finitely many entries.

Now suppose, for contradiction, that \(N\) had a representation of the required kind:
\[
N=a^2+b^2+B(c)+B(d),
\qquad a,b,c,d\ge0,
\qquad a\le b,
\qquad c\le d.
\]
The preceding bound gives \(0\le c\le d\le15\). Subtracting the two binomial terms yields
\[
a^2+b^2=R_{c,d}=N-B(c)-B(d).
\]
Look at row \(c\) and the entry corresponding to column \(d\) in the table. It supplies a prime \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) whose exact exponent in \(R_{c,d}\) is odd. By the sum-of-two-squares obstruction, \(R_{c,d}\) cannot equal \(a^2+b^2\), a contradiction.

Thus \(800\,322\,180\) has no representation as
\[
a^2+b^2+\binom{2c+1}{c}+\binom{2d+1}{d}
\]
with \(a\le b\) and \(c\le d\). Consequently
\[
a(800\,322\,180)=0.
\]
Since \(800\,322\,180>1\), the assertion that \(a(n)>0\) for every integer \(n>1\) is false.
